title: Shared primitives
description: Every artifact schema consumes these. Nothing here is specific to one type. Adding a primitive is a decision (notes.md); re-inventing one inside a type schema is the failure this file exists to prevent. See #82.

artifactId.description: Stable identity for one artifact. Prefix names the type, so a trace reference is self-describing without a registry lookup — which is what makes #75's unresolvable-reference check possible at lint time rather than load time. The number is allocated once and never reused, including after deletion.

typePrefixes.description: NOT a validation keyword — the authoritative mapping from #38's sixteen types to their ID prefixes, kept here so the pattern above and the lint agree. Adding a type (#40) edits this file, deliberately.

traceLinks.description: A trace field. Always an array of artifact IDs, never a bare string — a field that is sometimes one and sometimes many is two shapes for every consumer. Each artifact schema declares its own named trace fields and annotates them with x-traceTarget; there is no generic 'relation' field, because #61 requires materiality to be declared per field and a relation buried in a value cannot carry one.

notApplicable.description: #45. An explicit n/a carrying a required reason, so the lint can count *unjustified* absences rather than empty ones. Use as one branch of a oneOf on any field that may legitimately not apply.

nonEmptyString.description: A string that is present. Whitespace-only is caught by the lint, not by the schema — JSON Schema cannot express it without a pattern that is worse than the rule.

documentStatus.description: Per-artifact status. #4 puts this in the artifact rather than the manifest: shape is project-level, status is document-level. The app writes this field; the agent writes the payload — which is exactly the two-writer case #78's lockfile governs.

materialityValues.description: NOT a validation keyword — the authoritative values for the x-materiality annotation (#61), which every property in every artifact schema must carry. structural: identity and trace edges. semantic: the payload a reader acts on. advisory: priority, ordering, estimate. cosmetic: rationale, notes, prose.

artifactEnvelope.description: The fields every artifact carries regardless of type. Referenced by allOf from each type schema so the envelope is written once.

type.description: The artifact type, spelled as in #38. Redundant with the ID prefix on purpose: the prefix is for humans and cheap checks, this is what consumers switch on.

schemaVersion.description: #50. The content schema version this artifact was written against. Bumped on a breaking change to content shape, never on a tool release.

status.x-cascade-note: Classified structural because superseded/retired must flag everything tracing here. draft->in-review->approved must NOT flag anything. #60's one-hop cascade therefore has to filter on the transition, not merely on the field. Recorded rather than solved.

title.description: Short human label. Not an identifier.
